g.text: Mappings, Special Functions ([x], {x}, sgn), 7 Indeterminate Forms, Sandwich Theorem, and Discontinuity Profiles
∃ x₁ ≠ x₂ such that f(x₁) = f(x₂).
E.g. f(x) = x², f(x) = sin x. Fails H-test.
Every y ∈ Codomain has pre-image x.
A function f: A ➔ B is strictly Invertible (f⁻¹ exists) IF AND ONLY IF f is BIJECTIVE (Both Injective & Surjective).
• Every vertical line x = c must intersect
graph in AT MOST ONE point.
Circle x² + y² = r² fails (2 intersections).
• Every horizontal line y = k must intersect
graph in AT MOST ONE point.
• Saw-tooth waveform; Discontinuous at x ∈ ℤ
• Algebraic: sgn(x) = x / |x| = |x| / x for x ≠ 0
The Golden Criterion of Limit Existence
lim_{x➔a} f(x) = L exists IF AND ONLY IF:
WARNING: 0/∞ = 0, ∞/0 = ∞, 0^∞ = 0, ∞^∞ = ∞ are DETERMINATE forms! Do NOT apply L'Hôpital to determinate forms!
If lim f(x)/g(x) produces 0/0 or ∞/∞, then:
• Verify 0/0 or ∞/∞ before EVERY repeated step.
Standard Maclaurin Truncation Shortcuts (Faster than L'Hôpital):
sin x ≈ x - x³/6 | cos x ≈ 1 - x²/2 | eˣ ≈ 1 + x + x²/2 | ln(1+x) ≈ x - x²/2 | tan x ≈ x + x³/3
When limit has form [1]^∞ with base f(x) ➔ 1 and exponent g(x) ➔ ∞:
If g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) in a deleted neighborhood of c, and:
lim_{x➔c} g(x) = lim_{x➔c} h(x) = L ⟹ lim_{x➔c} f(x) = L
• lim_{x➔a} f(x) exists and is finite.
• But f(a) is undefined OR lim f(x) ≠ f(a).
• Fixable by redefining f(a) = lim f(x).
• Both LHL and RHL exist as finite numbers.
• At least one of LHL or RHL is ±∞
• Curve blows up to vertical asymptote.
• Cannot be made continuous by any value.
• E.g. f(x) = 1/x at x = 0, f(x) = tan x at π/2.
• Function oscillates infinitely near x = a.
• Neither LHL nor RHL approaches any limit.
• Contrast: x • sin(1/x) IS continuous at 0!
